title: Published SIPP poverty dynamics and source editions
description: Complete selected-characteristic tables for the two 24-month periods, plus every Figure 5 rate for the 36-month period.
geography: United States; national longitudinal samples, not Ohio estimates
methodology: Episodic poverty means at least two consecutive months in poverty during the stated observation period. Chronic poverty means poverty in every month of that period. Published 24- and 36-month estimates have different opportunities to enter or remain in poverty. The 2019 working paper and 2022 report precede the July 24, 2025 corrected Social Security microdata; the separately published February 2024 corrected tables cover annual/monthly rates, not a replacement of these chronic/episodic tables. This dataset is an edition-labelled source reference.

source.title: Poverty Dynamics: An Overview of Longitudinal Poverty Estimates Produced by the United States Census Bureau
source.locator: Tables 1–2; P70BR-179 Figure 5; current SIPP correction notices
source.note: Published historical editions are retained explicitly. Later corrections are tracked in the source concordance.
